messages.author: 0111ed37d2662b85
messages.subject: models suitable for PMCMC
parts:
Hi all,

Thanks to the whole NIMBLE team as always for creating and maintaining a super useful piece of software.

My question is about the SMC features in nimble. I'm interested in implementing them for a SSM like the following, but I haven't had success yet. The model shown below is meant for tree rings, where x are the true annual tree diameters (and thus x[t] > x[t-1] for all t) and y are measurements with additive error. When I run the following code, I get traceplots that suggest acceptance rates of 0. I suspect there may be something about the model syntax that isn't quite right for PMCMC tools (or perhaps something more fundamental about the model). Many thanks in advance for your feedback/suggestions.

-Henry

library(nimble)
library(nimbleSMC)
set.seed(1235)
SSM_model <- nimbleCode({
  sdl_x ~ dgamma(2, 1)
  sd_y ~ dgamma(1, 2)
  dx[1] ~ dlnorm(meanlog = 0, sdlog = sdl_x)
  x[1] <- dx[1]
  y[1] ~ dnorm(mean = x[1], sd = sd_y)
  for(i in 2:t){
    dx[i] ~ dlnorm(meanlog = 0, sdlog = sdl_x)
    x[i] <- x[i-1] + dx[i]
    y[i] ~ dnorm(x[i], sd = sd_y)
  }
})
t <- 30
model <- nimbleModel(code = SSM_model, constants = list(t = t))
model$simulate()
truth <- model
model <- nimbleModel(code = SSM_model, constants = list(t = t), data = list(y = truth$y))
Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
## PF ----
PF <- buildBootstrapFilter(model, nodes = "dx")
CPF <- compileNimble(PF, project = model, resetFunctions = T)
## PMCMC ----
conf <- configureMCMC(Cmodel, nodes = NULL)
target <- c("sdl_x", "sd_y")
conf$addSampler(target = target, type = "RW_PF_block", pf = PF, adaptScaleOnly = FALSE,
                control = list(latents = "dx", pfNparticles = 1000))
conf$addMonitors("logProb_y")
mcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(mcmc, project = model, resetFunctions = T)
Cmcmc$run(1000, nburnin = 500)
samples_PF <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)
## plots ----
layout(matrix(1:3, 3, 1))
plot(samples_PF[, 'sd_y'], type = "l", ylim = range(samples_PF[, 'sd_y'], truth$sdl_x), ylab = "sd_y")
abline(h = truth$sd_y, col = "darkred", lwd = 2)
plot(samples_PF[, 'sdl_x'], type = "l", ylim = range(samples_PF[, 'sdl_x'], truth$sdl_x), ylab = "sdl_x")
abline(h = truth$sdl_x, col = "darkred", lwd = 2)
plot(rowSums(samples_PF[, grep("logProb_y", colnames(samples_PF))]), type = "l", ylab = "logProb_y")

messages.author: 0111ed37d2662b85
messages.subject: Re: models suitable for PMCMC
parts:
One other bit of potentially helpful info: When I build conventional RW samplers for all variables, everything seems okay. The updates are inefficient as expected (hence the desire for SMC), but they seem to converge the right place.

Thanks again!
Henry

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: models suitable for PMCMC
parts:
To close the loop here, this bug report brought to light a deficiency in the logic of the RW_PF_block sampler (which is provided in the nimbleSMC package).  The bug would not have caused incorrect results, but instead warning/error messages and a failure of the MCMC to converge.

This has been patched in a development branch of nimbleSMC, which can be installed using:

remove.packages("nimbleSMC")
library(remotes)
remotes::install_github("nimble-dev/nimbleSMC", ref = "update_RW_PF_block", subdir = "packages/nimbleSMC")
library(nimbleSMC)

We'll also aim to release an updated version of nimbleSMC at some point in the future.

Cheers,
Daniel
